cards.headline: The number that describes what you actually lived through.
cards.body: Average return is a summary written afterwards. Drawdown is the part you had to sit through. A portfolio can average 10% a year and still spend a decade below a number it already reached. That decade is where people quit.

cards.headline: Drawdown is the fall from a peak.
cards.body: Measure from the highest value the portfolio has ever reached down to its lowest point after that. Peak 100, trough 60, drawdown **40%**. Not from where you bought. From the best it ever was.

cards.title: One drawdown, start to finish
cards.caption: The line peaks in year 2, bottoms 40% lower in year 5, and does not see that peak again until year 11. Three years down. Six years back.

cards.prompt: Two funds both fell 30% from their peak. One was back to even in nine months, the other in seven years. Which drawdown was harder to hold?

options.label: Equally hard — the depth was the same

cards.explanation: Depth and duration are two different numbers. Depth tells you how much you lost. Duration tells you how long you had to keep believing. **Duration** is what wears people out, and it never shows up in an annual return figure.

cards.headline: The second number is time.
cards.body: Every drawdown has a depth and a length. Depth is a headline. Length is a daily experience: months or years of opening an account worth less than it once was, with nothing to show for waiting.
Describe a drawdown properly and you need three facts, not one. Miss any of them and you have not described it.

cards.headline: An average hides the worst stretch.
cards.body: A strategy that returned 12% a year says nothing about the year it fell 45%. The average is arithmetic done after the fact. The worst stretch is the thing that had to be survived in real time to earn it.

cards.title: Same finish, different road
cards.caption: Both portfolios turn 100 into 150 over eight years. The dashed one never falls. The solid one halves from its peak by year 4 and needs four more years to reclaim it.

cards.body: The worst drawdown is the **binding** constraint on any plan, because the bottom of it is the point where people [[1]].
cards.explanation: A plan only compounds while it is still running. The deepest, longest stretch is where it gets switched off, so it sets the real limit on how much risk a person can actually carry.

cards.headline: Flat is harder than fast.
cards.body: A fall of 30% that rebounds in six months is loud but short. A portfolio that drifts sideways below its old high for five years is quiet, and quiet is what breaks discipline. Nothing happens. Nothing keeps happening.

cards.summary: Drawdown measures the fall from peak to trough, and the time spent getting back.
bullets: Depth is measured from the highest value ever reached, not from your entry price.
Time to recover is the number people underestimate most.
An average return says nothing about the worst stretch it contains.

cards.insight: A strategy is only as good as the worst stretch you can sit through. The depth ends portfolios; the waiting ends investors.
